request.spec:
An OPEN claim can be part-settled: an amount and a button on the claim. The amount is split off
exactly as the split button does, and the new claim is settled at once by the signed-in user exactly
as the settle button does (going to PENDING when the clerk limit says so); a split or a settle that
would be refused refuses the whole action with an error on the claim and changes nothing; the
four-eyes rules and the proof rule are judged on the original claim (the new claim's opener is the
signed-in user, as with the split button, who may still part-settle).

agent.result_text:
Part-settle is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/settle/part`, defined in `…/claims/{claimId}/settle/part.POST.yml`. I first tried a one-segment name (`settle-part`), but the existing `{action}.POST.yml` route took those requests and refused them as unknown actions. A two-segment path avoids that.
- **Checks first, on the original claim:** a new `CheckClaimSettlePart` step runs the settle button's checks before anything is written. The claim must be OPEN and not deferred. The user's role must be allowed to settle. The user can't be the one who opened or last edited the claim. The proof rule applies to the original claim's due and proofs.
- **Split:** the split itself reuses the split button's own steps. Any split refusal (bad amount, role not allowed to open, closed period) also happens before any write. A refusal returns 400, shows `claim-error`, and leaves both the store and the audit file unchanged.
- **Settle:** a new `SettleSplitClaim` step settles the new claim, or makes it PENDING when the clerk limit says so. The rest reuses the settle button's save, batch, log, audit, watcher-notify and rollup steps. The audit lines come out in the order the spec expects: `CLAIM_SPLIT`, `CLAIM_OPENED`, `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS`, then `CLAIM_SETTLED`.
- **Front end:** `ClaimStatus.tsx` has a new amount field (`claim-settle-part-amount`) and a "Part-settle" button (`claim-settle-part`). It clears the error the same way the Split controls do.

**One change to existing behaviour.** Scenario 1 never uses part-settle, but it expects a claim settled in a bulk settle to keep its batch number (`1`) after a one-at-a-time re-settle. The old code cleared the batch in that case, which also contradicted its own doc comment. I changed `SaveClaimBatch` so that a one-at-a-time re-settle keeps the claim's batch, and updated the comments in that class and in `{action}.POST.yml` to match. A one-at-a-time settle still gets no batch.
